speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience floaters or photopsia along with the black spots, and have you noticed any pain or redness in the right eye? I also need to know your most recent CD4 count and viral load to assess the severity of your immunosuppression.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and Kaposi's sarcoma, I am concerned about opportunistic infections like CMV retinitis or toxoplasmosis. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy; REQUEST TEST: HIV Viral Load and CD4 Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4 Count: 36/mm3. HIV Viral Load: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages, combined with a CD4 count below 50, are classic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis
